program_name: Digital Skills for Sustainable Societal Transitions (Laurea Magistrale interateneo / M.Sc.)
teaching_language: Fully English-taught AND interuniversity (joint) degree. Case (1) + case (3) of the field definition apply simultaneously: the whole 2-year, 120-ECTS degree is delivered in English ('The Master's degree programme, entirely taught in English'; PoliTo key-information box: 'Language: English'), and it is a joint 'corso di laurea magistrale interateneo' between Politecnico di Torino (PoliTo) and Universita degli Studi di Torino (UNITO). It is hosted by DIST - the Interuniversity Department of Regional and Urban Studies and Planning (Dipartimento Interateneo di Scienze, Progetto e Politiche del Territorio), which is itself jointly owned by PoliTo and UNITO. DIST's own catalogue lists it as 'DIGITAL SKILLS FOR SUSTAINABLE SOCIETAL TRANSITIONS - LM91 (POLITO/UNITO)', with POLITO named first, i.e. Politecnico di Torino is the administrative seat. Practical consequence for applicants: the whole admission and enrolment procedure runs on Apply@polito (polito.it), NOT on Apply@UniTo. The programme is NOT listed among the 26 English-taught postgraduate programmes searchable on apply.unito.it for a.y. 2026/27 (verified by an exhaustive filtered search of the Apply@UniTo catalogue), although UNITO does publish the degree in its own course catalogue at https://www.unito.it/ugov/degree/39572 . There is no Italian-language version of this degree and no Italian pathway/curriculum inside an Italian-named degree - it is a stand-alone English degree.
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy. Teaching campus: Castello del Valentino, Viale Pier Andrea Mattioli 39, 10125 Turin - the seat of DIST, the Interuniversity Department of Regional and Urban Studies and Planning (PoliTo/UNITO). Administratively the programme belongs to the Politecnico di Torino 'Architecture Area' (Collegio di Pianificazione e Progettazione).
degree_class: LM-91 - 'Metodi e tecniche per la societa dell'informazione' / 'Methods and Techniques for the Information Society'. Internal codes: Politecnico di Torino course code 81-473 (catalogue key 81:83); University of Turin course code 0902M21. 120 ECTS over 2 years. [uncertain]
admission_type: Open access / uncapped (no numero programmato, no ranking-based selection call), with mandatory verification of admission requirements. PoliTo's key-information box for the programme states: 'Admissions: Uncapped number of students, evaluation of the admission requirements'. The programme is NOT among the PoliTo master's programmes that require a competitive selection call for 2026/27 (only Nanotechnologies for ICTs-MNIS, Physics of Complex Systems and Ingegneria della Produzione Industriale e dell'Innovazione Tecnologica have such calls). Two distinct admission tracks exist: (a) applicants with a NON-ITALIAN qualification - document-based evaluation through Apply@polito in one of two annual calls, assessed first by the Recruitment and Admissions Unit (formal completeness) and then by an Academic Committee (academic performance + curricular consistency); no entrance test. (b) applicants with an ITALIAN qualification - application through Apply@polito in the Architecture Area rounds, with automatic admission if the curricular requirements (ECTS in listed disciplinary sectors) and the weighted-average-grade threshold are met, and a compulsory admission test in the form of an interview only for those who do NOT meet the weighted-average threshold. Admission is open in both the first and the second semester (unusual for PoliTo - most Architecture Area programmes are first-semester only). Applications for admission are also accepted from candidates who have not yet graduated (non-Italian track: at least 180 ECTS / 15 years of schooling; Italian track: at least 140 ECTS by July 2026).
application_deadline_eu: There is no separate EU-only call: PoliTo splits its calls by TYPE OF QUALIFICATION (Italian vs non-Italian), not by citizenship. (B) EU applicants holding a NON-ITALIAN qualification use exactly the same two international calls as non-EU applicants (see application_deadline_non_eu): 1st call 19 December 2025 - 13 February 2026, 2:00 p.m. Italian time (extended from 29 January 2026 by decree DR 96/2026); 2nd call 18 March 2026 - 20 April 2026, 2:00 p.m. Italian time (extended from 2 April, then postponed from 17 to 20 April due to technical problems). entry_exam_or_test: Depends on the track. (A) Applicants with a NON-ITALIAN qualification: NO entrance test and NO interview. The programme's own FAQ states: 'Do I need to pass an entrance test? No. International candidates are selected through evaluation of documents only'. Admission is decided by an Academic Committee purely on the submitted documents (transcript, degree, syllabus, language certificate). No portfolio is required for this programme (unlike the PoliTo Architecture and Urban Planning master's programmes), and the syllabus/course descriptions are marked 'Syllabus Optional' in the official 2026/2027 course-specific requirements table. (B) Applicants with an ITALIAN qualification: an admission test IS required, but ONLY for candidates who do not meet the weighted-average-grade threshold described under academic_requirements. The test is an ORAL INTERVIEW assessing academic performance, covering: action programmes for achieving the sustainable development goals; strategies and initiatives for the digital transition in urban agendas; basic elements of information technology; elements of territorial information systems. For 2026/2027 it is held in person at 2:00 p.m. in Aula Astengo, Castello del Valentino - on 8 September 2026 for first-semester admission (results 10 September 2026) and on 27 January 2027 for second-semester admission (results 29 January 2027). Results are published in the 'Evaluations' section of the candidate's Apply@polito page. Applicants with disability or a specific learning disability (DSA) may request support from the Special Needs Unit. [uncertain]
academic_requirements: GENERAL (all applicants): a Bachelor's degree (EQF level 6) or equivalent qualification giving access to second-cycle studies, plus 'suitable academic performance', plus curricular requirements, plus English B2. The programme is uncapped, so there is no fixed number of places and no non-EU quota published. NON-ITALIAN QUALIFICATION TRACK: (1) hold a Bachelor's degree (EQF 6) or equivalent awarded by an accredited foreign university, obtained after at least 15 years of previous education (primary + secondary + university); an 'equivalent academic qualification' means being enrolled in a foreign 5- or 6-year single-cycle programme, not yet graduated, with at least 15 years of global schooling (minimum 3 years at university level) and at least 180 ECTS or equivalent (pre-university/preparatory years excluded). (2) Meet curricular and quality requirements; an Academic Committee verifies the adequacy of the candidate's preparation and the consistency between the M.Sc. and the previous university career. (3) Recommended background per the official A.Y. 2026/2027 COURSE-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS table (field of study: Territorial Sciences): Information Technology and Computer Sciences, Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Architectural Engineering, Urban Engineering, Urban Planning, Civil Engineering, Building Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Economics and Accounting, Public Policy and Public Management, Media and Arts, Geography. The programme explicitly states that 'a background in computer science and ICT is welcome but it is not required' and that 'Students with a background in any field of Engineering, Architecture, Communication and Media Studies, Economics, Environmental and Geographic Sciences, Public Management, Social Sciences, Urban and Regional Planning, are recommended to apply.' No minimum GPA is published for this track ('Do I need to have achieved a minimum score at the end of my previous curriculum? To be considered eligible ... candidates must comply with the requirements (previous education + language) listed every academic year'), but a GRE General Test score report may be uploaded as an optional document to strengthen the application. ITALIAN QUALIFICATION TRACK (a.y. 2026/27, Architecture Area): CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS are expressed as minimum ECTS in two groups of Italian disciplinary sectors - 1st GROUP, minimum 25 CFU: MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/07, MAT/08, MAT/09, FIS/01, ING-INF/05, INF/01, ING-IND/35, IUS/10, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SPS/04, SPS/08, SPS/10 (new codes: MATH-02/B, MATH-03/A, MATH-04/A, MATH-05/A, MATH-06/A, PHYS-01/A, PHYS-03/A, IINF-05/A, INFO-01/A, IEGE-01/A, GIUR-06/A, ECON-02/A, ECON-06/A, ECON-07/A, GSPS-02/A, GSPS-06/A, GSPS-08/B); 2nd GROUP, minimum 45 CFU: ICAR/06, ICAR/08, ICAR/12, ICAR/14, ICAR/18, ICAR/20, ICAR/21, ICAR/22, L-ART/06, M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02, SPS/07, SPS/09, SECS-P/01, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/10, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/06, ING-IND/10, ING-IND/11, ING-IND/16, ING-IND/22, M-PSI/01, M-STO/04 (new codes: CEAR-04/A, CEAR-06/A, CEAR-08/C, CEAR-09/A, CEAR-11/A, CEAR-12/A, CEAR-12/B, CEAR-03/C, PEMM-01/B, GEOG-01/A, GEOG-01/B, GSPS-05/A, GSPS-08/A, ECON-01/A, ECON-04/A, ECON-09/A, ECON-08/A, STAT-01/A, STAT-02/A, STAT-04/A, IIND-07/A, IIND-07/B, IIND-04/A, IMAT-01/A, PSIC-01/A, HIST-03/A). Credits of a sector present in both groups count first towards Group 1, residual credits towards Group 2, and a single course's credits may be split between the two groups. If at most 10 credits are missing the Academic Advisor may admit the candidate anyway; if more than 10 are missing the file goes to the Coordinator/Deputy Coordinator of the Collegio. ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE (Italian track): applicants from universities other than the University of Turin need a weighted average grade >= 25/30, calculated on all graded credits (out of 30) counting towards the Bachelor's degree after subtracting the worst 28 credits, without rounding; applicants from the Universita degli Studi di Torino are admitted if time-to-graduation <= 4 years regardless of average, or 4-5 years with average >= 24/30, or > 5 years with average >= 25/30. Candidates who do not meet these thresholds must sit the admission interview. Applicants who lack curricular requirements can enrol in 'single courses for unfulfilled academic requirements' (only if 60 credits or fewer are missing) and must pass those exams before enrolling in the master's. Italian-track applicants may apply before graduating provided they have earned at least 140 ECTS by July 2026.
language_requirements: English at CEFR B2 minimum; no Italian language requirement (the programme is entirely in English). The official 'A.Y. 2026/2027 COURSE-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS' table sets the minimum score for this programme at IELTS 5.5 (the PoliTo B2 threshold). PoliTo's general rule for English-taught master's programmes is 'English level B2 or higher'. Accepted certificates and minimum scores per the PoliTo table of 23/09/2019 (last updated January 2026): IELTS Academic or General Training 5.5; Pearson Test of English Academic 59; TOEFL iBT 72 if taken before 21/01/2026, or 'Total 4' if taken on/after 21/01/2026 (new scoring scale); TOEIC Listening 400 / Reading 385 / Speaking 160 / Writing 150; Cambridge English B1 Preliminary (PET), B2 First (FCE), B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage), C1 Advanced (CAE), C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher), C2 Proficiency (CPE) all with a score of 160 on the Cambridge scale (older pre-2015/2016 formats accepted with specific thresholds and a Statement of Results). Paper-based, computer-based and online sittings are accepted, as are retakes of individual components. Administrative notes: for TOEFL/TOEIC you must enter PoliTo's code C285; for Cambridge you must share your results with PoliTo and provide your Candidate ID number. EXEMPTIONS from an English certificate: holders of an IB Diploma taught entirely in English (except foreign-language subjects); holders of a European School diploma whose first language (L1) is English; holders of a qualification recognised as equivalent to the Italian diploma di maturita (or higher) awarded by the USA, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand; and holders of such a qualification obtained after an English-medium learning path in a long list of countries (incl. India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Singapore, Malaysia, Malta, Cyprus, Jamaica, etc.); in these cases an official statement that the medium of instruction is English must be uploaded. TIMING: you may submit the application without the certificate, but it is a mandatory admission requirement and must be uploaded by the enrolment deadline. Italian-track candidates without a certificate may enrol in 'single courses for unfulfilled language requirements' (first semester only) and must present the certificate by 22 February 2027, otherwise they cannot enrol in any master's programme for 2026/27; PoliTo's Language Centre (CLA) organises IELTS sessions at reduced cost. NO Italian certificate is required for this English-taught programme (Italian B2 is required only for Italian-taught or partly Italian-taught PoliTo programmes).
required_documents: Apply@polito, applicants with a NON-ITALIAN qualification (a.y. 2026/2027) - compulsory documents are marked *: (1) Passport* (other IDs accepted only for EU nationals; only Latin-alphabet IDs, otherwise an official English/Italian translation); (2) Residence permit* (only for non-EU citizens living in Italy); (3) Curriculum Vitae* (any format); (4) Bachelor's degree certificate (EQF level 6)*, or, if not yet graduated, an official university document stating the provisional graduation date or an updated Transcript of Records; (5) Official Transcript of Records* (scanned front and back, listing all exams and including the grading system - minimum/maximum grade, final grade, GPA/CGPA - and the credit system; if missing, an official declaration from the Registrar's Office); (6) Syllabus / course descriptions - for THIS programme the 2026/2027 course-specific requirements table marks it as 'Syllabus Optional'; (7) Portfolio - NOT required for this programme; (8) English language certificate* (or an official statement of English medium of instruction if exempt); (9) Dichiarazione di valore or CIMEA Statement of Comparability (optional at application stage but compulsory for enrolment); (10) Self-certificate of enrolment in another Italian university, if applicable, including passed exams; (11) 'Other Document' (maximum one) - optional but recommended to strengthen the application: GRE General Test score report, recommendation letter, motivation letter, certificates of relevant training/internships, or proof of relevant work experience. Format rules: documents must be on letterheaded paper, stamped and signed by the issuing institution; digitally signed documents only if verifiable online via QR code or verification link; documents in Italian, English, French or Spanish are accepted, otherwise the original and its official translation must be merged into one file; PDF recommended (JPEG/PNG accepted); no hard copies are sent by post. A non-refundable application fee of EUR 50 must be paid online by credit card (VISA/MasterCard) via PagoPA. Incomplete applications are rejected and cannot be resubmitted in the same academic year. AT ENROLMENT the following are additionally compulsory: passport (or ID for EU students), residence permit (non-EU living in Italy), type-D study visa (non-EU not living in Italy, by 30 November 2026), Italian fiscal code certificate, Bachelor's degree with official Italian translation (not needed if the original is in English/French/Spanish or if a Diploma Supplement is provided), Transcript of Records with official translation, Declaration of Value / CIMEA Statement of Comparability / Diploma Supplement / ARDI 'Attestato di Corrispondenza', and the language certificate. Enrolment documents must be uploaded to the Teaching Portal by 5 October 2026 and are verified by 11 November 2026. ITALIAN-QUALIFICATION TRACK: registration on Apply@polito, selection of up to two master's programmes in order of priority, payment of the application fee (only for applicants from other Italian universities), plus graduation date and final grade entered in the 'Educational Background' section; no portfolio is required for this programme.

uncertainty_notes: 1) SPECIAL-CASE SCOPE: This is a joint (interateneo) LM-91 degree of Politecnico di Torino and the University of Turin, hosted by the jointly-owned DIST department. Per the task brief, polito.it and digitalskills.polito.it were treated as permitted primary sources for this item only. The single most decision-relevant finding for an admissions dataset is that ADMISSIONS ARE RUN ENTIRELY BY POLITECNICO DI TORINO, not UNITO: the programme is absent from the Apply@UniTo (DreamApply) catalogue for a.y. 2026/27 (verified by an exhaustive filtered POST search of apply.unito.it/courses/results), and every deadline, requirement and document list published for it lives on polito.it and the Apply@polito portal. UNITO publishes the degree only in its own read-only course catalogue (unito.it/ugov/degree/39572). If this record is merged into a UNITO-centric dataset, that asymmetry must be flagged to end users, or they will look for a non-existent UNITO application route. 2) DEAD MICROSITE: the programme website given in the task brief, https://digitalskills.polito.it/en, no longer resolves in DNS (NXDOMAIN, confirmed against 8.8.8.8 and via WebFetch, 1 September 2026). Its Requirements / Deadlines / FAQ pages were recovered from the Internet Archive (latest capture 27 October 2025). Content drawn from those captures (the 15-years-of-schooling rule, the 'no entrance test for international candidates' FAQ answer, the recommended-background list) is consistent with the current polito.it pages but is not live-verifiable; the recommended-background list on the microsite differs in wording from the official 2026/2027 course-specific requirements PDF, and the PDF should be treated as authoritative. 3) UNITO PAGES UNREACHABLE: www.unito.it and en.unito.it return Cloudflare 403 challenges from this environment, and the Internet Archive itself has only captured the challenge page for unito.it/ugov/degree/39572, so UNITO's own wording about the degree could not be read directly. The UNITO course code 0902M21, the LM-91 class and the 2-year/120-ECTS structure attributed to that page come from search-engine indexing of it, not from a direct read - hence degree_class is marked uncertain even though LM-91 is independently confirmed by polito.it and dist.polito.it. 4) EU vs NON-EU DEADLINES DO NOT MAP CLEANLY: unlike UNITO, PoliTo does not split its calls by citizenship but by type of qualification (Italian vs non-Italian). EU citizens holding a foreign Bachelor's degree therefore use the SAME two international calls as non-EU applicants, while EU (and non-EU) citizens holding an Italian Bachelor's degree use the domestic Architecture Area rounds. The application_deadline_eu field records both routes; do not read it as an EU-reserved call. 5) ALL 2026/2027 DEADLINES HAVE PASSED at the research date (1 September 2026) except the domestic second-semester round (applications 11 December 2026 - 18 January 2027) and the domestic first-semester enrolment deadline (2 November 2026). No 2027/2028 dates were published yet. The 2026/27 international deadlines were extended twice (decree DR 96/2026 +15 days, plus a technical postponement of the 2nd call to 20 April 2026), so the published pattern is a poor predictor of exact 2027/28 dates. 6) ENTRY TEST AMBIGUITY: the answer to 'is there an entrance exam?' genuinely depends on the applicant. International (foreign-qualification) applicants: no test at all. Italian-qualification applicants: an interview, but only if the weighted-average threshold is not met. The scheduled test dates (8 September 2026 / 27 January 2027, Aula Astengo) belong exclusively to the Italian-qualification track. 7) TWO DIFFERENT ACADEMIC ADVISORS are named on the same polito.it page (key-information box: Torabi Moghadam Sara; contacts block: Fabrizio Di Mascio, referente.lm.DIGITALSKILLS@polito.it); both are reported as-is. 8) NO PORTFOLIO / NO QUOTA: unlike the neighbouring PoliTo Architecture and Urban and Regional Planning master's programmes, this programme requires no portfolio, has no numero programmato, no ranking list and no published non-EU quota; a GRE score is optional and only strengthens an application. 9) TUITION: no programme-specific fee figure is published; only the general PoliTo rules (GDP-PPP-scaled fee for non-EU citizens with a EUR 600/year floor, plus the EUR 50 application fee). The linked Tuition Fee Regulations PDF found via search is the A.Y. 2025/2026 edition; the 2026/2027 edition is referenced from the enrolment pages but was not retrieved, hence the field is marked uncertain.
